$comment: CARI scoring contract. Values transcribed from DATA_SOURCES.md section 9.1. Where the old code and old comments disagreed, section 12 says the code values are correct and those are what appear here. Do not retype any of this into source code.
$sourcePriorityNote: Order the resolver walks to source a variable whose sourceModel is 'auto': it takes the first model here that actually catalogues the variable's band. PMD-WRF is preferred, then ECMWF-IFS, then ICON, then GFS, with GRAPES as the final backstop for the fields only it serves (precipitable water). Wind and vertical velocity exist only under GFS, so they land there; TCWV lands on GRAPES; everything else resolves to PMD-WRF.

variables.label: Precipitable Water
variables.$leadFallbackComment: GRAPES serves precipitable water empty at its 12-hourly synoptic steps (leads 0, 12, 24, ...) but populated at the 3-hourly steps in between. Precipitable water changes slowly, so when the target lead comes back empty the scorer substitutes the nearest lead that has data rather than grading a real primary input as zero.

terrainReduction.$comment: How elevation and slope get from a native DEM onto the scoring grid. Extracted from app.py lines 1431 to 1444 and repeated identically at 1730, 2054, 2159, 2648, 2902, 3216 and 3487. This is NOT a performance detail, it changes the numbers. Slope is computed FROM the 5 km reduced DEM, not from the native DEM. Slope measured over a 5 km run is far gentler than the same terrain measured over 30 m, so reproducing this with gdaldem on a native DEM would inflate every mountain district. See .claude/memory/slope-is-computed-at-5km.md.

scalarPath.$comment: Used by every district level score: CARI scalar, hotspot counts, susceptibility, alerts.

steps.$note: slope is derived HERE, on the 5 km grid

perPixelPath.$comment: Used only by the per pixel CARI raster. Native resolution DEM and slope, because the tile pipeline samples per zoom and the EE pixel cap does not apply. Reducing terrain to 28 km here was the documented cause of the whole district rendering as one flat color.

matrixSelection.$comment: Business rule, not data. Province names are compared after lowercasing and stripping non-letters. Districts loaded through scripts/ingest/ingest_admin.py already carry the canonical province name, so the short forms here are a second line of defence for any caller passing a raw source string. Missing one is silent: the district scores against the lowlands matrix and simply comes out lower. The district layer spells the disputed territory IOJK and the tehsil layer says FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY, and neither was in this list.

primaryExtremeOverride.$comment: Counts primary variables grading at or above gradeAtLeast. Raises the class floor only, never lowers it.

precipitationGate.$comment: Precipitation is the foundation of the index: convective ingredients only translate to risk where rain is actually forecast. After the class is decided (including the primaryExtremeOverride), if the region's peak forecast rainfall rate (the RF variable, the differenced mm/hr precipitation the scorer already reads) is below thresholdMmHr, or RF is missing entirely, the class is capped at capClassIdx and the reported percentage is capped to that class's ceiling. It runs last so a dry, high-CAPE district cannot be floored high by the override. Applies identically to the district and tehsil choropleth, the drill-down, the alerts feed and the per-pixel CARI raster, because all of them score through cari.py. Set enabled false to score without the gate. thresholdMmHr and capClassIdx are the only knobs; capClassIdx indexes classes[].

alerts.$comment: Districts at or above this class index enter the alert feed.

$scoreSourceNote: sourceBand is the wx.raster_catalog band a variable is read from; band stays the canonical key for display range and reference. sourceModel is 'auto' for a forecast field, meaning resolve the model by sourcePriority against what the catalogue actually carries, or null for a static field (elevation, slope). Today that resolves to PMD-WRF for RF, CAPE, RH700, RH500, DP, T2M and T850, GRAPES for TCWV (the only model serving precipitable water), and GFS for wind and vertical velocity. Each variable resolves against its own model latest cycle at the requested lead, so cross-source inputs align by lead when both feeds are current.
